opportunities.howToStart: Apply at houstonlibrary.org/youth-volunteer (online form). Allow up to 6 weeks for processing. Contact hplvolunteers@houstontx.gov or 832-393-1481.

opportunities.name: Children's Museum of Houston — Discovery Squad
opportunities.description: Discovery Squad is a year-long youth leadership program for ages 14-17 at Children's Museum Houston (Museum District) and the Fort Bend Children's Discovery Center (Sugar Land). Squad members assist with exhibits, activities, and programs — gaining hands-on experience facilitating science, art, and early-literacy programming for younger visitors. Selection is competitive (application + interview). Members commit to a minimum of 75 hours of volunteer service across the summer or school year. Distinct from the Museum's general Individual Volunteer pool, which accepts age 13+ with first-shift parent accompaniment. Discovery Squad is widely cited among Houston ISD/HISD-area college-prep counselors as a strong leadership/community-service entry. Applications for the 2026-27 cohort open April 2026.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply via volunteer.cmhouston.org → Discovery Squad. Selection is competitive (application + interview). Contact Dulce Aguirre, Office and Logistics Coordinator, at DAGUIRRE@cmhouston.org. Applications open annually in April.

opportunities.name: Houston SPCA Volunteer (Animal Care, Adoptions, Wildlife Center)
opportunities.description: Houston SPCA, founded 1924, operates a 7-acre campus in West Houston serving more than 35,000 animals each year — including Texas's largest 24/7 Wildlife Center. Teen and adult volunteers support animal care (feeding, exercise, socialization), adoption events, customer service at the front desk, special events, and the Wildlife Rescue program. Minimum age 16 at time of application. Ages 16-17 pay a $25 application fee that covers screening and a volunteer T-shirt; volunteers 18+ must complete a background check. Available shifts run 7 days/week, 7am-6pm, after completing orientation and training. Strong fit for teens interested in veterinary medicine, animal welfare, wildlife rehabilitation, or non-profit operations.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply at houstonspca.org/get-involved/volunteer (16+; $25 fee for under-18). Complete orientation + training before first shift. Wildlife Rescue program has separate application path at houstonspca.org/wildlife-center/volunteer-wildlife-rescue.

opportunities.name: Central Texas Food Bank Volunteer (Warehouse, Kitchen, Mobile Pantry, Garden, Youth Ambassador)
opportunities.description: Central Texas Food Bank is the largest hunger-relief charity in Central Texas, serving 21 counties from a 135,000 sq ft Austin facility. Tiered age policy: warehouse food-sorting shifts welcome volunteers 8+ (with adult 21+ supervision for under-15), Mobile Food Pantry distributions welcome 12+, kitchen and farm/garden shifts require 15+. The Youth Ambassador Program adds a separate sustained-engagement track for youth as young as age 5+ (with committed adult mentor) and culminates in independent shifts for older teens. Group requests up to 30 accepted for warehouse sorting. Strong fit for repeating school-year shifts (one weekly 3-hour slot is the norm).
opportunities.howToStart: Visit centraltexasfoodbank.org/get-involved/volunteer and create a volunteer profile. Pick a shift type matching your age (warehouse 8+, mobile pantry 12+, kitchen/garden 15+). For sustained engagement, apply to the Youth Ambassador Program at centraltexasfoodbank.org/youth-ambassador-program. Groups should email volunteer@centraltexasfoodbank.org to coordinate up to 30-person warehouse sessions.

opportunities.name: Austin Public Library Teen Volunteer Program (Seasonal Cohorts)
opportunities.description: The Austin Public Library Teen Volunteer Program runs three seasonal cohorts each year (Fall: Oct-Dec, Spring: Mar-May, Summer: Jun-Jul) for teens ages 13-17 (must be 13 by season cutoff and not yet 18). Volunteers commit to one 2-hour shift per week, typically supporting Youth Services librarians with circulation, in-branch programs, and program preparation across APL's branch network. Application windows are tight: Fall apps due July 1-31, Spring apps due Dec 1-31, Summer apps due Mar 1-31. Volunteers 17+ are also eligible to apply through the Adult Volunteer Program. Coordinator: Paul Lopez, APL.Volunteers@austintexas.gov.
opportunities.howToStart: Watch library.austintexas.gov/volunteer for the next open application window (deadlines: Jul 1-31 for Fall, Dec 1-31 for Spring, Mar 1-31 for Summer). Submit the online application during the open window and request the optional Volunteer Accommodation Request Form if needed. Direct questions to APL.Volunteers@austintexas.gov.

opportunities.name: Austin Pets Alive! Volunteer (Dog/Cat Care, Adoptions, Medical Clinic)
opportunities.description: Austin Pets Alive! is the largest no-kill animal shelter in the U.S. and a national leader in lifesaving animal welfare. Volunteer roles span dog walking, cat socialization, kitten foster support, parvo puppy ICU, behavior team support, adoptions counselor, transport coordination, and special-event support across the Austin Town Lake campus, Tarrytown campus, and other sites. Tiered age policy: 12+ minimum (12 must be accompanied by parent/guardian at all times), 13-15 require both volunteer + parent application, 16-17 may obtain a signed parental waiver to volunteer independently, 18+ no parental approval needed. Onboarding fee + online orientation + in-person site orientation required for each location.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit austinpetsalive.org/volunteer/requirements and review age-tier rules. Submit the volunteer application (parent must also submit if 12-15; signed parental waiver required if 16-17 to volunteer solo). Pay the onboarding fee, complete the online orientation video + quiz, then attend in-person orientation at each site you plan to serve. Once onboarded, browse open shifts via the APA! BetterImpact volunteer portal.

opportunities.name: Thinkery VolunTeen Program + Counselor-in-Training (Austin Children's Museum)
opportunities.description: Thinkery, Austin's children's museum (rebranded from the Austin Children's Museum in 2013), runs a structured 'VolunTeen' program for ages 13-18: volunteers receive 60 hours of personal/professional development training and give 40 hours back to the museum supporting STEAM-based exhibits and family programs. In a recent year, 208 VolunTeens served 8,880 hours. The Counselor-in-Training (CIT) program engages students entering 7th-12th grade to co-lead Thinkery summer camps under staff mentors. For shorter-term engagement, quarterly Teen Participation Days train teens on a single full-day shift (behind-the-scenes + on-the-floor). Excellent fit for STEM-curious teens and prospective educators.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply online at thinkeryaustin.org/support-us/volunteer/ for the VolunTeen track (13-18, 60-hr training + 40-hr service). For summer camp staff exposure, apply to the CIT program (entering 7th-12th grade). For lower-commitment engagement, watch the Thinkery events calendar for quarterly Teen Participation Days. The volunteer page is also reachable at thinkeryaustin.org/volunteer/.

opportunities.name: Caritas of Austin Community Kitchen Volunteer (Lunch Service for People Experiencing Homelessness)
opportunities.description: Caritas of Austin (founded 1965) ends homelessness for individuals and families in Austin/Travis County via housing programs, employment services, and the Community Kitchen. Community Kitchen volunteers prepare and serve lunch to ~250 people experiencing homelessness Monday-Friday 9:00am-1:30pm. Age policy: 13+ (under 18 must be accompanied by an adult). Onsite training is included in the shift; new volunteers arrive at 8:45am for orientation. A separate Direct Service Volunteer track (18+) commits to 6-8 hours/week for a minimum of four months alongside Caritas case managers, supporting clients moving into permanent supportive housing. 7-18 hours of 'Caritas University' training depending on Direct Service role.
opportunities.howToStart: For Community Kitchen (13+ with adult if under 18): visit caritasofaustin.org/get-involved/volunteer and sign up for one Mon-Fri shift 9:00am-1:30pm (arrive 8:45am the first day for orientation). For Direct Service (18+): contact volunteer@caritasofaustin.org to apply for the 4-month commitment with case managers. Group requests welcomed for Community Kitchen.

opportunities.name: North Texas Food Bank Volunteer (Pack & Box, Produce/Cold Sorting, Jan's Garden, Junior Kernel Program)
opportunities.description: North Texas Food Bank is the regional Feeding America-affiliated hunger-relief organization serving 13 counties around Dallas/Plano. Volunteer roles include Pack and Box (assembly-line meal packing — 12+, 12-15 with chaperone), Produce Sorting (16+, in 40°F cooler), Cold Sorting (16+, frozen/refrigerated dock), Jan's Garden (16+, on-site learning garden), Food Donation Door Clerk (18+), and Senior Food Box Distribution (18+). The Junior Kernel Program is a competitive 64-hour summer immersive for high school and college students (16-23) running May 26-August 8, with leadership and Kids Camp counselor pathways.
opportunities.howToStart: Register at ntfb.org/get-involved/volunteer and book individual or group shifts via the Volunteer Portal. For the Junior Kernel summer program, watch for spring application windows on the same page.

opportunities.name: Dallas Zoo — Zoo Crew Youth Volunteers + Adult Volunteer Corps
opportunities.description: The Dallas Zoo's volunteer program contributes over 100,000 service hours annually. Zoo Crew is a structured youth volunteer program for teens 13-17 interested in a zoo or animal-care career — placements span guest services, special events, education, and animal care, with an application + Zoo Crew Training Program required. Adult volunteers (18+, U.S. national, with social security number for background check) staff Animal Nutrition Center, Conservation Ambassadors (interpretive guest engagement using biofacts), Special Events, Special Projects (welders/carpenters/electricians), and Keeper Aide roles. Conservation Ambassadors and Animal Nutrition Center volunteers commit to one weekly shift.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply via dallaszoo.com/learn/volunteer (Zoo Crew has a separate application + training program). Email Volunteers@DallasZoo.com or call 469-554-7453 for inquiries.

opportunities.name: Dallas Public Library Volunteer + Teen Advisory Council (TAC)
opportunities.description: The Dallas Public Library accepts volunteers age 14 and older across its branches. Roles include Book Master (shelving, sorting, weeding, display creation, branch logistics), Events and Programming Collaborator (event prep + day-of support), and Court-Ordered Volunteering (low-level non-violent misdemeanors). The Teen Advisory Council (TAC) is a teen-led program that creates engaging programs for Dallas teens — DIY YouTube videos, Teen Talk Safe Spaces, TikTok content, YA author chats, Summer Teen Kits, SMART Summer scavenger hunts, and branch-level volunteering. TAC participants earn volunteer hours useful for school and college applications.
opportunities.howToStart: Submit the Volunteer Application Form via dallaslibrary.org/about/volunteer. Contact the Volunteer Coordinator at 214-671-9206 or libvolunteers@dallas.gov for branch placements and TAC information.

opportunities.name: Perot Museum of Nature and Science — ConnecTEEN + Year-Round Volunteers
opportunities.organization: Perot Museum of Nature and Science
opportunities.description: The Perot Museum's volunteer program supports STEM education and visitor engagement at its downtown Dallas campus. ConnecTEEN is the application-only summer cohort program for students entering grades 10-12 — 5 cohorts of 2 weeks each (Mon-Fri 9am-4:30pm), running June through August, with workforce-readiness sessions, STEM-professional connections, and team-building. Cohort 1 starts early June; orientation precedes each cohort. Year-round volunteers (teens 14+, adults 18+) commit to a 10-hour/month minimum across placements: 3D Dinosaur, Discovery on the Spot, Guest Services, Traveling Exhibition Support, Exhibition Hall Support. ConnecTEEN is a required first step for teens who want to continue as year-round volunteers. Background checks required for all adults; the museum no longer accepts court-ordered service.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply via perotmuseum.org/about/volunteer. ConnecTEEN summer applications typically open in early spring; year-round application is a separate form. Email volunteers@perotmuseum.org for groups (10-15 volunteers).

opportunities.name: SPCA of Texas Volunteer (Shelter, Clinic, Community Events — Adult + Youth Tracks)
opportunities.description: The SPCA of Texas is the largest animal welfare organization in North Texas, with shelter, clinic, and community programs across the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex. Volunteer tracks: Adults 18+ (background check, $15 application fee), Youth 15-17 (independent shifts, $15 fee), Kiddos 10-14 (must be accompanied by an adult 18+ during every shift, $15 fee). Off-site cat-location volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Activities span shelter operations, clinic support, community education events, mobile adoption events, and dog/cat enrichment. Court-ordered service tracks have a $35 fee.
opportunities.howToStart: Submit an application via spca.org/support-us/volunteer/ways-to-volunteer (separate forms for 18+, 15-17, and 10-14). Call 214-461-1886 with questions. New volunteers register for orientation through the Volunteer Portal at spcatx.volunteerportal.org.

opportunities.name: Food Bank For New York City Volunteer (Pantry, Repack, Community Kitchen)
opportunities.organization: Food Bank For New York City
opportunities.description: Food Bank For NYC is the city's largest hunger-relief organization (501(c)(3), member of Feeding America), serving all five boroughs. Volunteer roles span Pantry Distribution (14+ with adult chaperone if under 18), Hunts Point Distribution Center Repack in the Bronx (14+, 2.5-hr shifts), Community Kitchen meal service (18+), Older Adult Center Support (18+), and the SNAP Call Center (18+, bilingual). Group volunteering for ages 10+ available with adult chaperone (1:5 middle / 1:10 high school ratios). Individual sign-up via volunteer.foodbanknyc.org/calendar.
opportunities.howToStart: Sign up at volunteer.foodbanknyc.org/calendar for individual shifts; for group volunteering of 10-25 email volunteer@foodbanknyc.org. Repack shifts at 355 Food Center Drive, Bronx; Community Kitchen at 252 W 116th St, Manhattan.

opportunities.name: WCS Discovery Guide Youth Volunteer Program (Bronx Zoo + 4 sister facilities)
opportunities.description: The Discovery Guide program is a structured educational youth volunteer program for ages 14-22 across all 5 WCS facilities in NYC: Bronx Zoo (16+ at Bronx specifically), Central Park Zoo, Prospect Park Zoo, Queens Zoo, and the New York Aquarium (Coney Island, Brooklyn). Discovery Guides engage zoo/aquarium visitors in fun, educational activities, assist with education programs, and support wildlife campaigns. Spring and summer cohorts; commitment varies by location. The companion Project TRUE (Teens Researching Urban Ecology) program for high school sophomores/juniors living in the Bronx is a separate research-track partnership with Fordham University.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply via bronxzoo.com/volunteering/discovery-guide-volunteer-program (or the equivalent page for each WCS facility). Bronx Zoo applicants must be 16+ at time of submission; other WCS sites accept ages 14+. Email questions to discoveryguide@wcs.org (Bronx), NYAvolunteers@wcs.org (Aquarium), CPZdiscoveryguides@wcs.org (Central Park).

opportunities.name: New York Public Library Teen Volunteer & Reading Ambassadors
opportunities.description: NYPL serves Manhattan, the Bronx, and Staten Island through 92 branches plus four research libraries. Volunteer roles include branch-level support (shelving, programs, summer reading), the Teen Reading Ambassadors program (peer book recommendations for ages 12-18 readers), and virtual volunteering opportunities. Volunteers must be at least 14 years old; under-18 applicants need a parent/guardian to complete the consent section of the application. Brooklyn Public Library and Queens Public Library run separate teen volunteer programs (note: not the same system as NYPL).
opportunities.howToStart: Visit nypl.org/help/about-nypl/volunteer to apply. Branch coordinators match volunteers to roles. For Teen Reading Ambassadors, see nypl.org/remote-learning-resources/teen-reading-ambassadors. Brooklyn (bklynlibrary.org/support/volunteer) and Queens (volunteer.queenslibrary.org) systems are separate.

opportunities.name: American Museum of Natural History (AMNH) Volunteer
opportunities.description: AMNH (Central Park West, Manhattan) is one of the largest natural history museums in the world. Adult volunteer roles support Visitor Services (Information Desk, Hall Explainer), Education programs, the Library, and special exhibitions. Minimum volunteer age is 16 (no upper limit). Time commitment is one-half day to several days per week for at least one year (some positions require longer). Applications via the volunteer portal. The companion Science Research Mentoring Program (SRMP) and paid teen internships are separate tracks for science-track high schoolers.
opportunities.howToStart: Complete the online application at amnh.samaritan.com (linked from amnh.org/about/careers/volunteer). After application review, AMNH staff will contact about specific openings matching your availability and interests.

opportunities.name: ASPCA NYC Volunteer (Adoption Center, Recovery & Rehabilitation Center)
opportunities.organization: American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (ASPCA)
opportunities.description: The ASPCA's NYC operations center on the Adoption Center (424 E 92nd Street, Manhattan) and the Recovery & Rehabilitation Center (R&R) for dogs recovering from cruelty cases. Adoption Center Shelter Support volunteers must be 16+ — distinct Adult (18+) and Youth (16-17) application tracks. Recovery & Rehabilitation Center is 18+ only. Tasks include cleaning, sanitizing dishes/cages, walking and socializing animals, and general support. Volunteers must be able to stand 3 hours unassisted and lift 35 lbs. ASPCA does not currently accept court-ordered service.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply via aspca.volunteerportal.org/nycvolunteers (Adult 18+) or /nycyouthvolunteers (Youth 16-17). Recovery & Rehabilitation Center has a separate application — see aspca.org/get-involved/volunteer/volunteer-aspca-recovery-rehabilitation-center.

opportunities.name: City Harvest Volunteer (Repack, Greenmarket Rescue, Mobile Markets, Office Projects)
opportunities.description: City Harvest is NYC's largest food rescue organization, delivering 90M+ lbs of rescued food a year to feed nearly 2M New Yorkers facing food insecurity. Volunteer roles span the Brooklyn Volunteer Center in Sunset Park (repacks), Greenmarket Rescues (collecting unsold farmer's-market produce), Mobile Markets (free produce distribution at NYCHA and partner sites), Food Show Rescues (event surplus pickup), Nutrition Education Projects, and office support. Tiered age policy: 6-9 with 1:4 adult ratio (limited shifts); 10+ at repacks with chaperone; 14+ Greenmarket Rescues; 16+ Mobile Markets and Office Projects; 18+ Food Show Rescues and Nutrition Education. Minors require parent/guardian release waiver and adult 21+ chaperone except for Office Projects.
opportunities.howToStart: Register at cityharvestvolunteers.civicore.com, complete the volunteer application, and sign up for a shift type matching your age tier. Minors must have parent/guardian sign the release waiver and bring a 21+ chaperone (except Office Projects). Greenmarket Rescues are the most accessible 14+ shifts.

opportunities.name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden — Garden Apprentice Program (GAP)
opportunities.description: GAP is BBG's flagship teen program: a competitive 4-tier apprenticeship in urban agriculture, horticulture, and environmental science at one of NYC's premier public gardens. Apprentices in grades 9-11 commit to a 9-month program (March-November) — once or twice a week during spring/fall and four days a week in summer. Tier 1 apprentices learn garden basics; advanced tiers lead workshops, mentor younger apprentices, and run community programming. Long-running program (since 1998), strong college-app signal for environmental/STEM students. 12th graders are not eligible (apply junior year for the senior-year cohort).
opportunities.howToStart: Apply at bbg.org/learn/gap (application typically opens in late fall for the following March cohort). Attend a GAP information session before applying. Email gap@bbg.org with questions. Open to all NYC-area students grades 9-11; Tier 1 is the entry point.

opportunities.name: Brooklyn Public Library Teen Volunteer (Teen Techies, Book Buddy, Teen Takeovers)
opportunities.description: BPL — the third-largest library system in the U.S. and serving 2.6M Brooklyn residents — runs three distinct teen volunteer tracks. Teen Techies (14-18) help branch patrons with technology, devices, and digital literacy. Book Buddy (12-18) pairs teens with younger readers for literacy support and read-alouds. Teen Takeovers Branch Council (16-19) is a paid internship-style program where high schoolers plan, organize, promote, and host after-hours public programs for other teens. General volunteer minimum is 12+; under-18 must have parent/guardian sign the consent section of the application.
opportunities.howToStart: Submit the BPL volunteer application at bklynlibrary.org/volunteer (online or print). Indicate program of interest (Teen Techies, Book Buddy, or general). Parent/guardian consent required for under-18. For Teen Takeovers Branch Council, watch bklynlibrary.org/support/volunteer/branch-council for the next paid cohort cycle (16-19 only).

opportunities.name: Queens Public Library Teen Central + Peer-to-Peer Service Collective (P2PSC)
opportunities.description: QPL — serving 2.4M Queens residents across 65+ branches — runs a year-round teen volunteer program through Teen Central (volunteer.queenslibrary.org). Teens 14+ may apply year-round for ongoing roles (homework help, branch events, technology support, summer reading program); 13-year-olds are eligible for select single-day projects. The Peer-to-Peer Service Collective (P2PSC) is a high-school leadership program (14-18) where teens propose and lead community service projects, workshops, and presentations through QPL branches. Teen Central is QPL's online hub for teens 13-19.
opportunities.howToStart: Create an account at volunteer.queenslibrary.org and browse opportunities under Teen Central or Under-18 listings. Submit application + parent/guardian consent for under-18. For P2PSC (high school leadership), check the P2PSC page for cohort timing — applications typically open in late summer for fall start.

opportunities.name: New York Botanical Garden — High School Explainers Program
opportunities.description: NYBG's Explainers Program is a competitive, tiered teen volunteer program at the 250-acre Bronx botanical garden. Each year 100+ high school students start as Explainers in the Everett Children's Adventure Garden, leading hands-on plant and ecology activities for visiting families and school groups. Advanced tiers build outdoor-education skills, environmental stewardship, and public-facing science communication; the program is a feeder pipeline into NYBG's GreenSchool teaching corps and college environmental-science programs. Long-running flagship NYC teen STEM volunteer track.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit nybg.org/learn/kids-teens/explainers/ for the application cycle (typically opens late fall/early winter for the following spring/summer cohort). Open to all NYC-area high school students; competitive admission. Contact NYBG Education for cycle-specific deadlines.

opportunities.name: Coalition for the Homeless — Grand Central Food Program (GCFP) Volunteer
opportunities.description: Founded 1981, the Coalition is the nation's oldest advocacy and direct-service organization helping homeless New Yorkers. The Grand Central Food Program is the largest nightly mobile soup kitchen in the country, delivering ~1,000 meals every night of the year at 22 stops across Manhattan and the Bronx. Volunteers help set up and serve at St. Bartholomew's Church (4:30-6:30pm) Monday-Friday, with consistent multi-week commitment expected. Drivers run the route 6:45-9:30pm (separate role; valid license / 21+ for vehicle insurance reasons). Kids and teens not yet ready for evening service can run school care-kit drives, back-to-school supply drives, or host the Coalition's Advocacy presentation. Note: explicit age min not published on the GCFP volunteer page — confirm directly via volunteer@cfthomeless.org.
opportunities.howToStart: Email volunteer@cfthomeless.org to request a GCFP shift. For school-based involvement (care kits, supply drives, presentations), see coalitionforthehomeless.org/how-kids-and-teens-can-help/. Note: GCFP requires consistent recurring attendance, not one-off shifts.

opportunities.name: New York Cares Youth-Friendly Volunteering (Family Friendly + Teen Friendly + Teen Group)
opportunities.description: NYC's largest volunteer-mobilizing organization, with a year-round youth-friendly tier explicitly designed for ages 5-17. Family Friendly projects let parents register children ages 5-13 and serve alongside them. Teen Friendly projects (ages 14-17) allow solo participation or with a parent/guardian. Teen Group projects bring 14+ teens together with a 21+ group leader for serving meals to the homeless, visiting seniors, tutoring younger kids, environmental cleanups, and arts events. Parent/guardian must create the New York Cares account first and register the youth to the family roster (one-time online waiver).
opportunities.howToStart: Parent/guardian creates an account at newyorkcares.org, registers the youth to the family roster, and signs the one-time online waiver. Then browse the calendar filtered by Family Friendly, Teen Friendly, or Teen Group.

opportunities.name: Greater Boston Food Bank Volunteer (Sort & Inspect, Kids Who Care, Families for Impact)
opportunities.description: GBFB is the largest hunger-relief organization in New England, distributing tens of millions of meals per year across Eastern Massachusetts. Standard sort-and-inspect warehouse shifts are 16+; volunteers under 18 require an adult chaperone. Group-based youth programs lower the bar: Kids Who Care welcomes group volunteers as young as 10, and Families for Impact runs exclusive family events for kids age 5+. Multiple shifts daily at the Yawkey Distribution Center in Boston.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit gbfb.org/get-involved/volunteer to register for an individual or group shift. Kids Who Care and Families for Impact have separate registration tracks. Email volunteer@gbfb.org for group bookings.

opportunities.name: Zoo New England — Summer ZooTeen + Teen Ambassador + Keeper Aide (Franklin Park Zoo / Stone Zoo)
opportunities.organization: Zoo New England (Franklin Park Zoo + Stone Zoo)
opportunities.description: Zoo New England operates Franklin Park Zoo (Boston) and Stone Zoo (Stoneham) with three distinct teen tracks: (1) Summer ZooTeen — ages 14-18, 6-week summer experience combining work in animal care, horticulture, marketing, and camp counseling with professional development and life-skills training. Paid ZooTeen roles are reserved for Boston and Cambridge residents; volunteer ZooTeen roles are open to all. (2) Teen Ambassador Program — ages 15-17, October-May, 15 hr/week, by application after completing ZooTeen. Designed for Boston youth interested in wildlife, education, and environmental justice. (3) Keeper Aide volunteer (16+) — three-hour shift weekly, 9am-12pm, supporting the Zoo Education team. No fee to volunteer at either zoo.
opportunities.howToStart: Summer 2026 ZooTeen application posts mid-March at zoonewengland.org/discover/teen-programs/summer-zooteen-paid/. Teen Ambassador admits select ZooTeen alumni. For Keeper Aide, email fpzvolunteers@zoonewengland.com.

opportunities.name: MSPCA-Angell Volunteer (Boston Adoption Center + Nevins Farm Junior Volunteer)
opportunities.organization: MSPCA-Angell (Massachusetts Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals)
opportunities.description: Founded 1868, MSPCA-Angell is one of the oldest humane societies in the United States. Two distinct volunteer tracks: (1) Boston Adoption Center & Angell Animal Medical Center — 16+ minimum (16-17 must obtain and submit a completed MA Youth Work Permit). Roles include animal care, adoption support, hospital reception, and veterinary observation. (2) Junior Volunteer Program at Nevins Farm Adoption Center (Methuen) — ages 11-15, with experienced volunteers and staff coaching participants. Summer Camp Junior Counselor positions at Nevins Farm require age 15 by start date (per MA state employment law). Northeast Animal Shelter (Salem) and Cape Cod Adoption Center are additional sites.
opportunities.howToStart: Boston: visit mspca.org/animal_care/frequently-asked-questions-boston-mspca-volunteer-program/ to apply (16+; MA Youth Work Permit for 16-17). Nevins Farm Junior Volunteer (11-15): apply via mspca.org/adoption-centers/nevins-farm-adoption-center/humane-education-programs-at-nevins-farm/junior-volunteer-program/.

opportunities.name: Boston Public Library Teen Volunteer Program
opportunities.description: Boston Public Library's flagship teen volunteer program, open to teens in grades 9-12 across 10 BPL sites (Central Library Teen Central + Children's Library, Brighton, Codman Square, Connolly, Grove Hall, Hyde Park, Mattapan, Roslindale, Shaw-Roxbury, West Roxbury). Teens learn customer service and library systems while assisting branch programs. The program runs year-round in fall (September-December) and spring (January-June), with optional skill-building Monday Zoom workshops (book review writing, BiblioCommons, etc.). Develops job-readiness skills.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply at bpl.org/teen-volunteer-program/. Open to all teens in grades 9-12. Volunteer for one semester (fall, spring, or summer) or year-round across 10 BPL sites. Contact Agneris Lopez at volunteer@bpl.org or 617.859.2304.

opportunities.name: Museum of Science, Boston — Youth Volunteers + Classic Volunteers
opportunities.description: Two-tier volunteer program at one of the largest science museums in the U.S. (Boston's Charles River campus, 700+ exhibits). Youth Volunteers are high-school-age (14-19) and assist exhibit floor educators, public programs, and Live Animal Care Center support. Classic Volunteers are 18+ and commit to a 4-month department-aligned tour (planetarium operations, exhibit interpretation, special events, IMAX theater, member services). Separate paid Summer Youth Internship program for 14-19-year-olds runs 7 weeks with weekly professional-development workshops and department projects.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply at mos.org/careers/volunteer. Youth Volunteers track is for ages 14-19 in high school; Classic Volunteers track is 18+ and requires a 4-month department commitment. The 7-week paid Summer Youth Internship (ages 14-19) is a separate competitive pathway with professional development workshops.

opportunities.name: New England Aquarium Volunteer + Live Blue Ambassadors
opportunities.description: Boston Central Wharf aquarium with 58,000+ volunteer hours per year supporting Aquarium operations and ocean-conservation education. General volunteer roles (Visitor Education / Exploration Station / behind-the-scenes department support) are 16+, with most positions requiring 18+. The Live Blue Ambassadors program is a teen-focused robust field-and-community-based conservation program with hands-on shoreline cleanups and education at local environmental sites. The separate paid Summer Teen Internship (ages 14+, Boston/Cambridge/suburbs residents) runs alongside.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply on rolling basis at neaq.org/engage/join-our-team/volunteer/. General volunteer minimum is 16 (most positions 18+). Live Blue Ambassadors is the teen track. The paid Summer Teen Internship is the entry path for ages 14-15. Contact volunteer@neaq.org with questions.

opportunities.name: Pine Street Inn Volunteer (Boston Homeless Services)
opportunities.description: Largest homeless-services provider in New England (founded 1969), operating emergency shelters, permanent supportive housing, and the iStreet Outreach van across Greater Boston. In-person volunteer roles include serving meals at Men's Inn / Women's Inn / Long Island Shelter, kitchen prep, donation sorting, and the Innbassador public-speaking corps. Remote volunteer opportunities (donation drives, advocacy, fundraiser support) are available with broader age accessibility.
opportunities.howToStart: Sign up at pinestreetinn.org/get-involved/volunteer/. In-person volunteers must be 18+. Remote volunteer opportunities (donation drives, advocacy, Innbassador-style public speaking, fundraiser support) accept younger volunteers. Contact Volunteer Department at 617.892.9184 or volunteer@pinestreetinn.org.

opportunities.name: Cradles to Crayons Boston (Giving Factory + Teen Leadership Corps)
opportunities.description: Boston-area nonprofit (Giving Factory warehouse in Newton, MA) providing essential clothing, books, and school supplies to children living in poverty. Year-round volunteer roles include Giving Factory shifts (sorting, inspecting, packaging KidPacks), Mobile Pop-Up Shops, donation drives, and the Teen Leadership Corps (TLC) for middle and high school students. Family-friendly: ages 5+ welcome with adult, and entire families volunteer side-by-side. Group volunteer pre-registration is available for school clubs / scout troops / corporate teams.
opportunities.howToStart: Sign up for Giving Factory shifts at cradlestocrayons.org/boston/take-action/volunteer/. Minimum age is 5; volunteers under 18 must have an adult present for the entire shift. Middle and high school students can join the Teen Leadership Corps for deeper service-learning engagement; group pre-registration is available for school/scout/corporate teams.

opportunities.name: Forgotten Harvest Volunteer (Distribution Center / Pop-Up Pantries / Farm Team)
opportunities.organization: Forgotten Harvest (Detroit / Oak Park / Fenton MI)
opportunities.description: Detroit-area food rescue nonprofit (founded 1990) that recovers and redistributes surplus food across Wayne, Oakland, and Macomb counties. Tiered teen-friendly volunteer roles include Distribution Center repacking and warehouse work (10+, under-18 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian), Pop-Up Pantry food distribution events at host sites (12+), Farm Team work at Forgotten Harvest Farms in Fenton (14+, planting/weeding/harvesting on a 92-acre regenerative farm), Harvest Heroes peer-advocate volunteers (14+ outside the warehouse), and 18+ Site Monitor / Long-Term volunteer track. Court-Ordered Community Service is accepted only at the Eight Mile warehouse. Online registration required via Galaxy Digital portal.
opportunities.howToStart: Register online at forgottenharvest.galaxydigital.com or via the volunteer page at forgottenharvest.org/volunteer-3/. Choose a shift at the Distribution Center (10+), a Pop-Up Pantry event (12+), a Farm Team day in Fenton (14+), or apply for the Harvest Heroes / Site Monitor / Long-Term roles (14-18+). All under-18 volunteers must be accompanied by a parent or guardian. For group registration email volunteer@forgottenharvest.org.

opportunities.name: Detroit Zoo Volunteen (Zoo Corps + Summer Zoo Corps + Counselor-In-Training)
opportunities.organization: Detroit Zoological Society (Royal Oak / Huntington Woods MI)
opportunities.description: Detroit Zoo's umbrella teen volunteer program for ages 14-17, run by the Detroit Zoological Society's Education department. Three tracks: Zoo Corps (year-round leadership + science communication, members are trained to facilitate hands-on activities exploring science, environmental stewardship, humane education, and animal information across the 125-acre Royal Oak campus), Summer Zoo Corps (summer-only cohort), and Counselor-In-Training (CIT, ages 15-17 supporting Summer Safari Camp by guiding youth groups, supervising craft projects, and interacting with guests). The Detroit Zoological Society also operates Belle Isle Aquarium and Belle Isle Nature Center. Applications for the 2026 CIT cohort opened in March 2026.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit detroitzoo.org/volunteer-opportunity/volunteen/ for current track openings. Email volunteer@detroitzoo.org or call 248-541-5717 ext. 3802. Zoo Corps is year-round; Summer Zoo Corps and CIT applications open seasonally (typically March for summer cohorts). All three tracks are unpaid and structured around education-department mentorship.

opportunities.name: The Greening of Detroit Volunteer (Tree Plantings + Green Corps Youth Program)
opportunities.description: Detroit-based urban forestry nonprofit (founded 1989) that has planted 177,000+ trees across Detroit, Hamtramck, and Highland Park. Two main pathways for teens: (1) general Volunteer Tree Plantings on Thursdays and Saturdays in spring (March-May) and fall (September-November), 9am-1pm at parks, schools, and neighborhoods across Detroit — open to individuals and groups, with a streamlined online registration; (2) Green Corps, an 8-week paid summer youth employment program for high school students ages 14-18 who maintain hundreds of trees and green spaces around Metro Detroit. Note: ageMin for the general tree planting events is not explicitly published on the volunteer page; Green Corps Youth Program is explicit at 14-18. Confirm directly with the organization for younger volunteers at general planting events.
opportunities.howToStart: Register for an upcoming tree planting at greeningofdetroit.com/volunteer (Thursdays and Saturdays, March-May and September-November). For the paid Green Corps Youth Program (ages 14-18, 8-week summer employment), apply via the Workforce Development > Green Corps page at greeningofdetroit.com. Email info@greeningofdetroit.com or call 313-237-8733 with questions. Note: general planting events do not publish an explicit minimum age — confirm with the org for younger participants.

opportunities.name: Michigan Humane Volunteer (Recurring + One-Time + Group)
opportunities.organization: Michigan Humane (Detroit / Westland / Sterling Heights / Rochester Hills / Howell)
opportunities.description: Michigan's largest animal-welfare nonprofit (founded 1877), operating Adoption Centers in Detroit, Westland, and Sterling Heights (Petco) plus Veterinary Centers in Detroit, Rochester Hills, and Westland. Two volunteer tracks: (1) Recurring volunteer roles for ages 18+ (4-month commitment minimum, 2-hour shift once per week, working directly with animals); (2) One-Time volunteer events open to ages 14-18 with a parent or guardian accompanying for the full shift, plus group volunteer days for school clubs / scout troops / corporate teams. Short-term volunteers do not work directly with animals (Dog Day Getaway and Straw Bagging are common one-time offerings). Adult chaperones accompanying youth must be 25+.
opportunities.howToStart: Browse upcoming one-time events at michiganhumane.org/one-time-volunteering/ — register for a Dog Day Getaway or Straw Bagging shift at Detroit, Westland, or Sterling Heights. For recurring roles (18+, 4-month commitment) email volunteerdepartment@michiganhumane.org. Teens 14-17 must volunteer with a parent or guardian; adult chaperones must be 25 or older.

opportunities.name: Henry Ford Hospital Detroit Volunteer (Year-Round Adult + Summer High School)
opportunities.description: Volunteer program at Henry Ford Hospital, Henry Ford Health's flagship academic medical center on West Grand Boulevard in Detroit. Year-round roles (18+, minimum 4 hours/week) include patient companion / way-finding / gift shop / spiritual support / Gift of Music / Transplant Living Community (TLC) peer support / Hospice / Observation-Shadow. The hospital also runs a Summer High School Volunteer Program (parallel to the Henry Ford West Bloomfield 16-17 summer program and the Henry Ford Jackson Hospital Summer Youth Program for current high school students who have completed at least their freshman year) and a Henry Ford Cancer - Detroit High School Volunteer Program. Note: the Detroit summer-program age minimum is not published explicitly on the volunteer page; the Henry Ford system summer youth programs at sister sites use 16+ (West Bloomfield) and post-freshman HS (Jackson) — confirm directly with the Detroit Volunteer Services team.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply at henryford.com/locations/henry-ford-hospital/volunteer/apply-request. Year-round adult roles require 18+ and 4 hours/week; the Summer High School Volunteer Program and Henry Ford Cancer - Detroit High School Volunteer Program admit current high school students. Contact Volunteer Services at the Detroit campus to confirm age eligibility for the summer programs (the Detroit page does not publish the explicit minimum). Application portal: vsyslive.hfhs.org.

opportunities.name: Food Gatherers Volunteer (Warehouse + Community Kitchen)
opportunities.description: Founded 1988 as the first food rescue program in Michigan and a program of Jewish Family Services, Food Gatherers is Washtenaw County's primary food bank and only mobile food rescue program — distributing 10.3M+ pounds of food annually via a working warehouse at 1 Carrot Way and a Community Kitchen serving hot meals 7 days/week. Volunteers sort/repackage food and prep meals via individual or group registration on a 3-month rolling shift calendar (foodgatherers.volunteerhub.com).
opportunities.howToStart: Create individual user account or submit Group Registration form at foodgatherers.org/get-involved/volunteer/. Shifts at warehouse: 8+ with adult, 14+ alone. Community Kitchen: 12+ with adult, 14+ alone. Hours-tracking accepted for school or court-ordered service. Phone: 734-761-2796.

opportunities.name: Ann Arbor District Library Teen + Adult Volunteer Program
opportunities.description: AADL runs a year-round teen + adult volunteer program supporting library programming and general operations across 5 branches (Downtown, Malletts Creek, Pittsfield, Traverwood, Westgate). Volunteers help with public programs and events; book shelving is paid staff. AADL also offers an online Points-O-Matic remote volunteering pathway. Coordinated via the BetterImpact application portal.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply at aadl.org/volunteer (BetterImpact portal). 14-17 must submit parent/guardian permission slip. 18+ background check required for certain tasks. Volunteer orientation required. Email volunteer@aadl.org.

opportunities.name: Feeding America West Michigan Volunteer (Warehouse + Repack)
opportunities.organization: Feeding America West Michigan (Comstock Park / Kentwood MI)
opportunities.description: The regional Feeding America food bank for West Michigan and the Upper Peninsula — partnering with 800+ agencies across 40 counties. Volunteers at the Comstock Park warehouse near Grand Rapids break down bulk food (cereal, diced carrots, Pop-Tarts) into family-sized portions, sort senior boxes, and repack produce. Common 2-3 hour shifts year-round.
opportunities.howToStart: Sign up at feedwm.org/volunteer/. 8+ may volunteer with adult chaperone (1:5 adult-to-youth ratio for 15-and-under); 16+ alone. All youth must be accompanied at all times in the warehouse.

opportunities.name: John Ball Zoo Youth Volunteer Team + Helper
opportunities.description: John Ball Zoo's 15-year-old Zoo Teen / Youth Volunteer Team places high-school-age volunteers in Guest Engagement roles across Guest Services and Education, with optional advancement to higher-commitment Animal Team roles. Teens learn to share information about the zoo's animals with the public and run interpretive carts. Programs run during summer with fall extensions.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply at jbzoo.org/volunteer/youth/. 14+ can volunteer independently as part of the Youth Volunteer Team (ages 14-17); 12+ can volunteer with an adult under the Helper program. Annual application window (apply early — competitive cohort).

opportunities.name: Humane Society of Huron Valley Junior Volunteer Program
opportunities.organization: Humane Society of Huron Valley (HSHV) — Ann Arbor MI
opportunities.description: HSHV's Junior Volunteer (JV) Program is a 6-session humane-education + hands-on cohort for ages 12-17. Trained graduates work assignments including cat comforting, dog visitation, shelter cleaning, humane-education support (camp counselor track), enrichment-toy crafting, and offsite events. JVs commit to 2-4 hours/month after the program and must come in at least once every 90 days to stay active. The 6-session program has a $195 fee covering training materials. Hours count toward school community service.
opportunities.howToStart: Register at hshv.org/volunteer-2-2/juniorvolunteer/. $195 program fee. After completing the 6-session JV program, schedule shifts at events.hshv.org. Email volunteers@hshv.org for questions.

opportunities.name: League of Women Voters Youth Volunteer
opportunities.description: Volunteer with local LWV chapters in voter registration drives, candidate forums, ballot information distribution, and youth civic education. Open to ages 14+ (some chapters allow 16+ as full members). Excellent for kids interested in civic engagement, public policy, and pre-law tracks. Year-round availability with peak activity around elections.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit lwv.org and find your local chapter via zip code. Most chapters welcome HS volunteers for voter registration drives + youth civic education programs. Apply Aug-Oct for election-year activity peak.

opportunities.name: Generation Citizen Action Civics
opportunities.description: Generation Citizen runs an action civics program in 100+ HS classrooms across NYC, Boston, San Francisco, Providence, Oklahoma. Students identify local issue + advocate for change with local officials. Volunteer roles include classroom co-teacher, mentor, and chapter leader for HS students who've completed the program. Excellent pre-law + public policy pipeline.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit generationcitizen.org/get-involved. HS students who completed GC curriculum can apply to be Civics Action Mentors for younger cohorts. Apply Aug-Sep for school year programming.

opportunities.name: Common Cause Voter Engagement
opportunities.description: Common Cause is one of America's oldest nonpartisan good-government organizations (founded 1970). HS volunteer roles include voter registration outreach, redistricting advocacy support, voting rights education, and election protection (poll monitoring at age 18+). 35+ state chapters with active student programs.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit commoncause.org/take-action and select your state chapter. HS volunteer roles available year-round, with election-year peaks Aug-Nov.

opportunities.name: Local Community Theater Volunteer (national network)
opportunities.description: AACT serves 7,000+ community theaters nationally. Volunteer roles for HS students 14+: ushering, set construction, costume design, lighting + sound assistance, stage management, props, marketing, fundraising. Most local theaters welcome HS volunteers and provide hands-on technical training. Excellent for theater + arts-track students.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit aact.org and use the theater locator to find theaters in your area. Email volunteer coordinator OR show up to open auditions/work calls. Most welcome teens with interest + enthusiasm.

opportunities.name: NPR Member Station Youth Volunteer
opportunities.description: 600+ NPR member stations welcome HS volunteers age 16+ for tasks like phone bank during pledge drives, station event support, transcription, social media outreach, and youth advisory boards. Excellent for journalism + media-track students. Some stations run formal high school journalism programs (KQED Youth Voices, WBUR Field Notes, etc.).
opportunities.howToStart: Find your local NPR member station at npr.org/stations and email their volunteer coordinator. Larger stations (KQED, WBUR, WNYC) have formal HS journalism programs — apply early (Sep-Dec).

opportunities.name: Mikva Challenge Youth Civic Action
opportunities.description: Mikva Challenge runs civic action programs in Chicago, DC, LA, NYC, Cleveland, San Francisco. HS students 14+ participate in election-cycle internships, issue-to-action projects, and policy fellowships. Pipeline to high-quality civic engagement roles + Mikva Alumni Network. Strong fit for kids interested in elected office or public policy careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit mikvachallenge.org/get-involved and apply for a fellowship in your city. Chicago + DC are flagship; programs available in 6 cities. Apply Aug-Oct for school year, Mar-May for summer.

opportunities.name: American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) Student Member
opportunities.description: ACLU has 50+ state affiliates with student volunteer programs. HS roles include rights education outreach, civil liberties advocacy at school, voter registration drives, and First Amendment + Fourth Amendment student journalism support. Strong fit for pre-law + journalism students.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit aclu.org and select your state affiliate. Most welcome HS volunteers for rights education + outreach. Some state ACLUs run formal Youth Advisory Boards — apply Sep-Dec for school year programs.

opportunities.name: Local NAACP Youth Council
opportunities.description: NAACP has 1,200+ youth + college chapters nationally. HS-aged students (12-18) join Youth Councils for civil rights advocacy, voter education, criminal justice reform support, and community organizing. Pipeline to NAACP National Youth + College Division leadership conferences. Strong fit for civil rights + pre-law track.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit naacp.org/find-your-local-branch and contact your local NAACP branch about Youth Council. School-affiliated and community Youth Councils available. Apply Aug-Oct for school year programming.

opportunities.name: Junior State of America (JSA)
opportunities.description: JSA is a nonpartisan student-run civic engagement organization with 800+ HS chapters across the US. HS students lead chapters, organize debate tournaments, attend regional + national conventions, and engage in policy advocacy. Pipeline to JSA Summer Schools (Princeton + Stanford + Georgetown campus programs). Strong fit for debate + politics + pre-law students.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit jsa.org/find-a-chapter to see if your school has a chapter (or start one). Apply Aug-Oct for school year. JSA Summer Schools at Princeton/Stanford/Georgetown have separate Mar-Apr application.

opportunities.name: Young Americans for Liberty (YAL) Chapter
opportunities.description: YAL is a libertarian youth organization with 800+ chapters at HS and college levels. HS roles include chapter founding + leadership, policy education, voter outreach, and YAL National Convention attendance. Strong fit for libertarian-leaning + small-government conservative students. Pipeline to YAL Mises Institute fellowships + Cato Institute internships.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit yaliberty.org/start-a-chapter to start one or yaliberty.org/find-a-chapter to join existing. Apply Aug-Oct for school year activity.

opportunities.name: NAMI Walks Volunteer + NAMI on Campus HS
opportunities.description: NAMI has 600+ state + local affiliates with active HS volunteer programs. HS roles include NAMI Walks event coordination, NAMI on Campus HS chapter founding, mental health education outreach, and Stigma Free advocacy. Excellent for kids interested in psychology, social work, or pre-med psychiatry careers. Year-round availability with peak NAMI Walks May-Oct.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit nami.org/find-your-local-nami and contact your local affiliate. NAMI on Campus HS chapters can be started at most schools — see nami.org/oncampus. Apply Aug-Oct for school year.

opportunities.name: JED Foundation Student Mental Health Volunteer
opportunities.description: JED Foundation focuses on emotional health + suicide prevention for teens + young adults. HS volunteer roles include JED+ Comprehensive Mental Health Education campaigns at school, peer-to-peer Set To Go transition program, Mental Health Resource Center outreach, and #SeizeTheAwkward campaign ambassadorship. Strong fit for psychology-track students.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit jedfoundation.org/get-involved and apply to be a JED+ ambassador or Set To Go peer leader. Year-round availability.

opportunities.name: Active Minds Student Chapter
opportunities.description: Active Minds has 800+ student-led chapters across HS + colleges nationally. HS chapter members lead mental health awareness events, peer-to-peer support training, suicide prevention campaigns, and Speaker Series participation. Strong fit for psychology + public health + social work-track students.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit activeminds.org/start-chapter to found a chapter at your school OR find existing at activeminds.org/find-a-chapter. Apply Aug-Oct for school year.

opportunities.name: To Write Love On Her Arms (TWLOHA) Chapter
opportunities.organization: To Write Love On Her Arms
opportunities.description: TWLOHA focuses on hope + help for those struggling with depression, addiction, self-injury, suicide. HS volunteer roles include UChapter founding, World Suicide Prevention Day events, Heavy + Light campaign ambassadorship, and peer-to-peer hope outreach. Strong cultural fit for music + arts-oriented students (TWLOHA founded via music industry).
opportunities.howToStart: Visit twloha.com/uchapters to start a UChapter at your HS. Year-round availability with peak World Suicide Prevention Day Sep 10 + Mental Health Awareness Month May.

opportunities.name: The Trevor Project Volunteer (LGBTQ Youth Crisis)
opportunities.description: The Trevor Project provides crisis intervention + suicide prevention services to LGBTQ youth (under 25). Volunteer roles include digital crisis counselor (must be 18+, formal training), TrevorSpace community moderator (16+), peer-to-peer outreach, fundraising, and student advocacy. Strong fit for LGBTQ+ allies + future mental health professionals.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit thetrevorproject.org/volunteer. Most direct crisis counselor roles require age 18+, but TrevorSpace moderator + ally outreach available at 16+. Year-round application.

opportunities.name: RAINN (Rape, Abuse + Incest National Network) Volunteer
opportunities.description: RAINN operates the National Sexual Assault Hotline. Volunteer roles for those 18+ include hotline support, RAINN Speakers Bureau (Survivor Storytellers), and online chat moderation. HS-aged students (16+) can volunteer with school-based prevention education campaigns + RAINN Day campus advocacy. Strong fit for pre-med, pre-law, social work students.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit rainn.org/volunteer-rainn. Hotline + chat counselor roles require 18+ + 50-hour training. HS-aged students can volunteer with prevention education campaigns + RAINN Day school activities.

opportunities.name: Mental Health America (MHA) Affiliate Volunteer
opportunities.description: MHA has 200+ state + local affiliates nationwide. HS volunteer roles include mental health screening event support, May Mental Health Awareness Month campaigns, peer-to-peer outreach education, and MHA's Back-To-School Toolkit distribution. Strong fit for kids considering psychology or psychiatry careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit mhanational.org/find-affiliate and contact your local MHA affiliate. Year-round availability with peak May (Mental Health Awareness Month). Apply Aug-Oct for school year.

opportunities.name: Boys Town National Hotline Support
opportunities.description: Boys Town operates a National Hotline (1-800-448-3000). Direct hotline counselor roles require 18+, but HS volunteer roles available include Boys Town Saving Lives Volunteer Drive coordination, Behind the Scenes administrative + event support, and Save the Date fundraising. Strong fit for pre-med + social work-track students.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit boystown.org/volunteer. Year-round availability with peak holiday season (Nov-Dec) + spring (April).

opportunities.name: Crisis Text Line Counselor (18+)
opportunities.description: Crisis Text Line provides 24/7 text-based crisis intervention. Direct counselor roles require 18+ + 30 hours training (typically college students + adults). HS-aged students 14-17 can volunteer with Crisis Text Line ambassador programs at school + summer ambassador programs. Strong fit for kids planning psychology + clinical mental health careers — pipeline to formal counselor role at 18+.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit crisistextline.org/become-a-volunteer. Direct counselor role at 18+. Ambassador role at 14+ — see ambassador.crisistextline.org. Year-round application.

opportunities.name: Bring Change to Mind HS Chapter
opportunities.description: Bring Change to Mind (founded by actress Glenn Close) runs HS-specific chapters (formerly U Bring Change 2 Mind) at 400+ high schools nationally. HS chapter members lead mental health awareness campaigns, anti-stigma classroom education, and peer-to-peer mental health support. Strong fit for kids interested in psychology + advocacy careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit bringchange2mind.org/learn/high-school-program to start a chapter at your HS. Apply Aug-Oct for school year programming.

opportunities.name: Translators Without Borders Volunteer
opportunities.description: Translators Without Borders provides language services to humanitarian organizations globally. HS volunteer roles for bilingual students 16+ include translation projects (Spanish, French, Arabic, Mandarin, Portuguese, etc.), language learning support, and outreach. Strong fit for bilingual students considering international relations, linguistics, or humanitarian careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit translatorswithoutborders.org/volunteer-with-us. Apply via online portal — bilingual fluency required. Year-round availability.

opportunities.name: Operation Smile Student Programs
opportunities.description: Operation Smile runs cleft lip + palate medical missions globally + HS student programs. HS roles include Operation Smile Club founding at school, Mission Possible fundraising, International Student Leadership Conference attendance, and Surgical Missions Volunteer (18+). Pipeline to medical mission internships. Strong fit for pre-med + global health-track students.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit operationsmile.org/get-involved/students. Start an Operation Smile Club at your school OR apply for International Student Leadership Conference (Sep-Nov apps for following spring conference).

opportunities.name: Heifer International Read-to-Feed + Youth Programs
opportunities.description: Heifer International ends global hunger + poverty by giving livestock + agricultural training to communities. HS volunteer roles include Read-to-Feed school book club fundraising, World Ark youth ambassador, Heifer Village internship (18+ Arkansas), and global service trips (organized through schools). Strong fit for kids interested in international development + sustainable agriculture.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit heifer.org/give/youth. Read-to-Feed school programs available year-round. Heifer Ranch internships (Perryville AR) require 18+. Apply Aug-Oct for school year programming.

opportunities.name: World Vision Student Ambassadors
opportunities.description: World Vision runs HS student ambassador program with 30 Hour Famine fundraising, child sponsorship awareness, advocacy on child poverty + clean water + education. Strong Christian + faith-based context. HS roles include school chapter founding, 30 Hour Famine event coordination, and global advocacy. Strong fit for faith-track students interested in international service.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit worldvision.org/youth-ministry/30-hour-famine. Start a 30 Hour Famine team at your school OR church. Apply Aug-Oct for school year planning.

opportunities.name: Plan International USA Youth Advocates
opportunities.description: Plan International USA focuses on girls' rights + education globally. HS Youth Advocate program for ages 14-18 includes Girls Get Equal advocacy campaigns, social media outreach, school chapter founding, and International Day of the Girl (Oct 11) event coordination. Strong fit for girls-rights + international development-track students.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit planusa.org/youth-advocates. Apply Aug-Sep for school year programming.

opportunities.name: Save the Children Student Activist
opportunities.description: Save the Children Action Network runs HS Student Activist program for ages 14-18. Roles include Capitol Hill Day advocacy (visit Members of Congress), Tax Code education + child poverty advocacy, school chapter founding, and global child rights campaigns. Pipeline to humanitarian + public policy careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit savethechildrenactionnetwork.org/youth-engagement. Apply Aug-Sep for school year. Capitol Hill Day events Mar-May.

opportunities.name: Global Citizen Year Bridge Year Pre-Engagement
opportunities.organization: Global Citizen Year (now part of Bard College)
opportunities.description: While Global Citizen Year main program is a gap year between HS + college, the GCY Pre-Engagement program for HS students 14-18 includes monthly virtual seminars, global affairs discussions, Bridge Year alumni mentor matching, and admission counseling for the gap year program itself. Strong fit for kids considering deferred college + global service careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit globalcitizenyear.org/get-involved. Pre-engagement program available year-round; main gap-year application deadline Sep-Dec for following year.

opportunities.name: Doctors Without Borders Junior Activist
opportunities.organization: Doctors Without Borders / Médecins Sans Frontières (USA)
opportunities.description: Doctors Without Borders runs HS Junior Activist program for ages 14-18. Roles include school chapter founding, advocacy campaigns on humanitarian access, Refugee Crisis education, and World Refugee Day (Jun 20) event coordination. Pipeline to MSF medical careers (most direct medical roles require MD + 2 years residency, but advocacy + administrative roles available earlier).
opportunities.howToStart: Visit doctorswithoutborders.org/take-action. Junior Activist program available year-round; apply Aug-Oct for school year campaigns.

opportunities.name: Engineers Without Borders USA Student Chapter
opportunities.description: Engineers Without Borders USA has 250+ student chapters at universities + 350+ professional chapters. HS volunteer roles include EWB-USA Student Chapter founding (some HS chapters exist), volunteer engineering project support, and Annual Conference attendance. Pipeline to undergraduate EWB chapters at top engineering schools. Strong fit for engineering-track students interested in international development.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit ewb-usa.org/get-involved. HS chapters require school sponsor + 5+ founding members. Apply Aug-Oct for school year programming.

opportunities.name: Habitat for Humanity Global Village
opportunities.description: Habitat for Humanity Global Village sends US volunteers globally to build homes (typically 1-2 weeks abroad). HS-aged students can join Habitat Youth Programs at school + community level (build with local Habitat affiliate; international Global Village trips typically require 18+). Strong fit for kids interested in housing justice + international service.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit habitat.org/volunteer. Local Habitat affiliates welcome 14+ for community builds. Global Village international trips typically 18+.

opportunities.name: Meals on Wheels America Volunteer
opportunities.description: Meals on Wheels America has 5,000+ local programs delivering meals to homebound seniors. HS volunteer roles include food packing, delivery driver assistant (for parent-teen pairs), Friendly Visitor companionship calls, and Meals on Wheels Pet Loaf program. Strong fit for kids interested in senior care + community service.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit mealsonwheelsamerica.org/find-meals to find your local program. Most local Meals on Wheels welcome HS volunteers (under 16 typically requires parent/guardian). Year-round availability.

opportunities.name: Feeding America Network Volunteer
opportunities.description: Feeding America operates 200+ food banks + 60,000+ partner agencies nationally. HS volunteer roles include food bank sorting + packing, Backpack Program (weekend meals for kids), Mobile Pantry distribution, and Hunger Action Month (Sep) campaigns. Strong fit for kids interested in food justice + public health.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit feedingamerica.org/find-your-local-foodbank. Most local food banks welcome HS volunteers — younger kids often need parent/guardian. Apply year-round.

opportunities.name: Food Recovery Network Student Chapter
opportunities.description: Food Recovery Network is the largest student-led nonprofit fighting food waste + hunger nationally. 230+ college chapters + growing HS chapter network. HS volunteer roles include school-based food recovery program founding, dining hall + cafeteria food rescue, and food donation logistics. Strong fit for kids interested in environmental sustainability + food justice.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit foodrecoverynetwork.org/start-a-chapter. Apply Aug-Oct to start a chapter at your HS for school year programming.

opportunities.name: World Central Kitchen Disaster Relief Volunteer
opportunities.description: WCK (founded by Chef José Andrés) provides meals during disasters globally. HS volunteer roles vary based on operations — typically food packing, fundraising, social media advocacy. Direct disaster-zone deployment requires 18+. WCK Chefs for America HS-friendly events available year-round. Strong fit for kids interested in culinary + disaster relief careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit wck.org/get-involved. Direct disaster deployment 18+. HS-aged volunteer roles include fundraising + Chefs for America events. Year-round.

opportunities.name: Family Promise Affiliate Volunteer
opportunities.description: Family Promise has 200+ affiliates nationally helping families experiencing homelessness through congregation-based shelters + transitional services. HS volunteer roles include Day Center activity coordination with kids in shelter, donation drive organizing, school supplies distribution, and after-school tutoring at affiliate sites. Strong fit for kids interested in homelessness advocacy + social work.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit familypromise.org/find-an-affiliate. Most affiliates welcome HS volunteers — congregation-based affiliates often easier entry point. Year-round.

opportunities.name: Loaves & Fishes Network Volunteer
opportunities.description: Loaves & Fishes operates 150+ regional food + meal programs nationally (Northern California, Sacramento, Annapolis MD, Naples FL, etc.). HS volunteer roles include daily meal service prep + serving, food pantry sorting, garden + farm-to-table program support, and special events. Strong fit for kids interested in hunger + food systems.
opportunities.howToStart: Search 'Loaves and Fishes [your city]' to find your regional Loaves & Fishes. Most welcome HS volunteers + younger kids with parent/guardian. Year-round.

opportunities.name: Project Bread Walk for Hunger Volunteer (Boston)
opportunities.description: Project Bread is Boston's leading anti-hunger nonprofit (founded 1969). HS volunteer roles include Walk for Hunger (annual May event with 8,000+ walkers), FoodSource Hotline support (18+), school-based hunger awareness campaigns, and Tackle Hunger NFL partnership events. Strong fit for Boston-area kids interested in food justice.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit projectbread.org/get-involved. Walk for Hunger registration opens Jan-Apr; year-round volunteer opportunities at Boston HQ.

opportunities.name: Wednesday's Child Adoption Awareness Volunteer
opportunities.description: Wednesday's Child is a national TV news segment (since 1981) featuring children awaiting adoption. Local volunteer roles include adoption awareness fundraising, foster + adoption family support, post-adoption transition services, and respite care for foster families. HS-aged volunteers can support school-based foster care awareness campaigns. Strong fit for kids interested in social work + child welfare.
opportunities.howToStart: Search 'Wednesday's Child [your state]' to find your regional program. Most affiliated with state child welfare offices. Year-round.

opportunities.name: DC Central Kitchen Junior Volunteer
opportunities.description: DC Central Kitchen is the nation's first community kitchen (founded 1989) producing 5,000+ meals daily for shelters + schools. HS volunteer roles include daily meal prep + cooking with chefs (14+ requires guardian; 16+ unaccompanied), Healthy Corners corner store food distribution, and Culinary Job Training program support. Strong fit for kids interested in culinary + food justice careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit dccentralkitchen.org/volunteer. Year-round availability with peak holiday season (Nov-Dec).

opportunities.name: FareStart Junior Volunteer (Seattle)
opportunities.description: FareStart is Seattle's flagship culinary job training nonprofit (since 1992) for adults transitioning out of homelessness. HS volunteer roles include 2nd Saturday community meal service, Catalyst Kitchens youth programs, food packing for shelter partner agencies. Strong fit for Seattle-area kids interested in culinary careers + homelessness advocacy.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit farestart.org/get-involved. 2nd Saturday community meal service open year-round. Apply via online portal.

opportunities.name: Best Friends Animal Society Volunteer
opportunities.description: Best Friends operates Best Friends Animal Sanctuary (Kanab UT — largest no-kill sanctuary in US) + 200+ partner shelters nationally. HS volunteer roles include shelter dog/cat socialization, foster home care, transport drivers (with guardian), and Best Friends Sanctuary 1-week volunteer trips (16+). Strong fit for kids interested in animal welfare + veterinary track.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit bestfriends.org/get-involved/volunteer. Local network opportunities year-round; Sanctuary 1-week trips require 16+ + advance booking.

opportunities.name: Petfinder Foundation Affiliate Volunteer
opportunities.description: Petfinder Foundation supports 11,000+ animal welfare organizations across the US. HS volunteers can connect with local Petfinder member shelters for direct volunteering. Roles include shelter dog walking, cat socialization, adoption event support, and foster care assistance. Strong fit for kids interested in animal welfare careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit petfinder.com to search 11,000+ partner shelters in your zip code, then contact directly. Each shelter has its own age + volunteer requirements.

opportunities.name: Surfrider Foundation Beach Cleanup + Chapter Volunteer
opportunities.description: Surfrider Foundation has 90+ chapters across coastal + Great Lakes states. HS volunteer roles include Beach Cleanup Day organizing (October Coastal Cleanup), Ocean Friendly Restaurant program outreach, Plastic Pollution advocacy, and Coastal Defense campaigns. Strong fit for kids interested in marine conservation + environmental science careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit surfrider.org/get-involved/find-a-chapter. Most chapters welcome HS volunteers (under 14 typically with parent). Annual Coastal Cleanup Day in October.

opportunities.name: Ocean Conservancy International Coastal Cleanup
opportunities.description: Ocean Conservancy organizes the world's largest volunteer-led ocean cleanup event annually (International Coastal Cleanup, mid-September). HS volunteer roles include Cleanup Site Coordinator (16+), Ocean Defender campaign ambassador, Plastic Pollution advocacy, and Trash Free Seas Alliance research. Year-round opportunities at 100+ partner organizations nationally. Strong fit for marine + environmental science track.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit oceanconservancy.org/trash-free-seas/international-coastal-cleanup. International Coastal Cleanup peaks Sep — sign up Aug-Sep. Year-round campaign volunteer roles available.

opportunities.name: World Wildlife Fund Action Network
opportunities.description: WWF Action Network is the volunteer arm of WWF-US. HS volunteer roles include WWF Wild Classroom curriculum tutor, Earth Hour event coordination (annual March), petition outreach for endangered species protection, and Junior Conservationist online courses. Strong fit for environmental + biology + global affairs-track students.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit worldwildlife.org/take-action. Year-round campaign volunteer roles. Earth Hour annual March; Junior Conservationist courses available year-round.

opportunities.name: TreePeople Los Angeles
opportunities.description: TreePeople is LA's leading urban forestry nonprofit (founded 1973). HS volunteer roles include LA tree planting events (peak Jan-Mar + Oct-Nov), Wilshire Center tree care, school-based environmental education, and TreePeople Mountain leadership trips. Strong fit for LA-area kids interested in urban forestry + environmental science.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit treepeople.org/get-involved/volunteer. Year-round availability; tree planting peaks Jan-Mar + Oct-Nov.

opportunities.name: Conservation Volunteers International Program
opportunities.description: CVI sends US volunteers to conservation projects globally (Costa Rica, Galápagos, Borneo, Australia, Mexico). HS volunteer trips for ages 14+ include reef restoration, sea turtle conservation, primate research, and wildlife monitoring. Strong fit for kids interested in international conservation + biology fieldwork.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit conservationvip.org/student-trips. HS group trips arranged through schools or families; individual youth trips (14+) require advance booking. Apply Mar-May for summer trips.

opportunities.name: Trout Unlimited Chapter Volunteer
opportunities.description: Trout Unlimited has 400+ chapters nationally focused on coldwater fisheries conservation. HS volunteer roles include stream cleanup days, Trout in the Classroom school program support, fly tying classes, and Trout Camp summer experience (typically 12-18). Strong fit for kids interested in fisheries biology + sport fishing.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit tu.org/find-a-chapter. Most chapters welcome HS volunteers; Trout Camp typically Jul-Aug — apply Mar-May.

opportunities.name: American Farmland Trust Youth Volunteer
opportunities.description: American Farmland Trust protects farmland from development + supports sustainable agriculture. HS volunteer roles include Farmer School Day program organizing, Farmland Forever campaign outreach, school garden support, and Sustainable Agriculture Coalition advocacy. Strong fit for kids interested in agriculture, food systems, or environmental policy.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit farmland.org/take-action. Year-round campaign volunteer roles. Apply Aug-Oct for school year programming.

opportunities.name: Audubon Christmas Bird Count
opportunities.description: Audubon's Christmas Bird Count (CBC) is the world's longest-running citizen science project (since 1900). HS volunteer roles include CBC team participation in late Dec-early Jan annual count, Junior Audubon Society chapter founding, bird banding workshops, and Backyard Bird Count (annual Feb). Strong fit for kids interested in ornithology + ecology.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit audubon.org/conservation/science/christmas-bird-count. CBC takes place Dec 14-Jan 5 each year — register Nov for participation. Year-round chapter activities.

opportunities.name: Reading Is Fundamental Volunteer
opportunities.description: RIF is the largest US children's literacy nonprofit (founded 1966). HS volunteer roles include book delivery to schools + libraries, Read for Success book group leader, Skybrary online tutoring (16+), and RIF Volunteer Reading Day events. Year-round + peak during Read Across America Day (March 2). Strong fit for kids interested in education + literacy careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit rif.org/get-involved/volunteer. Year-round availability. Read Across America Day annual March 2 — peak need Feb-Mar.

opportunities.name: First Book Volunteer
opportunities.description: First Book has provided 235M+ books to kids in low-income communities. HS volunteer roles include book sorting + warehouse support (regional warehouses in Washington DC + Atlanta), book drive coordination at school, and First Book Marketplace promotional events. Strong fit for kids interested in literacy advocacy + nonprofit operations.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit firstbook.org/take-action. Apply year-round. Book drives can be organized at any school.

opportunities.name: Khan Academy Volunteer Tutoring + Translation
opportunities.description: Khan Academy provides free online education globally. HS volunteer roles include Khan Academy Translation team (translate lessons to other languages — strong fit for bilingual students), Math + Science answer review, course content tester, and content advisory committee. Strong fit for kids interested in education tech + global accessibility.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit khanacademy.org/about/blog/post/get-involved-translation. Translation roles year-round. Answer review + content review available — apply via online portal.

opportunities.name: College Possible Coach
opportunities.description: College Possible runs near-peer mentoring programs for low-income HS students applying to college. HS-aged students 16+ can serve as Coaches in their own school for younger students; college students serve as full mentors. Strong fit for kids interested in college counseling + education access careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit collegepossible.org/programs to find your local College Possible site (Chicago, Milwaukee, Minneapolis, Omaha, Philadelphia, Portland, Twin Cities). Apply Aug-Oct.

opportunities.name: Year Up Junior Volunteer Network
opportunities.description: Year Up provides career training to young adults (18-24). HS volunteer roles include school-based mentor recruitment, post-secondary readiness workshops in HS, Career Pathways advocacy, and Year Up campus visit hosting. Strong fit for kids interested in workforce development + career pathways.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit yearup.org/get-involved. Most direct mentor + career roles require 18+; HS volunteer roles available at school level.

opportunities.name: Boys Hope Girls Hope Junior Volunteer
opportunities.description: Boys Hope Girls Hope provides residential + nonresidential academic + life skills support to under-resourced kids ages 10-22.
