HS volunteer roles include after-school tutoring at affiliate sites, College Search visit hosts, Christmas Drive coordination, and Hope Day school visits. Strong fit for kids interested in education access + residential education.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit boyshopegirlshope.org/get-involved. Find your local affiliate (50+ cities). Year-round availability.

opportunities.name: Learning Ally Volunteer Audiobook Reader
opportunities.description: Learning Ally is a leading audiobook nonprofit for students with dyslexia + visual impairment. HS volunteer roles include Audiobook Studio Reader (recording educational audio — book chapters + textbooks), Learning Ally student support outreach, and dyslexia awareness campaigns. Strong fit for kids interested in special education + accessibility advocacy.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit learningally.org/volunteer. In-person studio recording at major Learning Ally cities (Princeton NJ, Athens GA, Cincinnati OH, Phoenix AZ); virtual recording also available. Year-round.

opportunities.name: OneGoal Junior Mentor
opportunities.description: OneGoal helps low-income HS students prepare for college + persist through completion. HS volunteer roles include OneGoal Fellow program (3-year experience for HS students 10-12 grade), peer mentorship, college essay support, and ACT/SAT prep. Strong fit for kids interested in education access + college persistence research.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit onegoalgraduation.org/get-involved. OneGoal Fellow program (3-year HS experience) requires application Aug-Oct of grade 10. Adult mentor roles 18+.

opportunities.name: Communities In Schools (CIS) Volunteer
opportunities.description: Communities In Schools is the largest dropout prevention organization in the US, working in 2,500+ schools nationally. HS volunteer roles include Site Coordinator support, peer-to-peer tutoring, Community Service Learning project leadership, and CIS Resource Drive coordination. Strong fit for kids interested in education access + dropout prevention research.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit communitiesinschools.org/get-involved. Find your local CIS affiliate (in 26 states + DC). Year-round availability.

opportunities.name: DonorsChoose Project Support Volunteer
opportunities.description: DonorsChoose connects donors with public school teachers seeking classroom funding. HS volunteer roles include School-Based Project Champion (organizing project funding for your own school's teachers), Project Promotion ambassador, Letter Writing for project pages, and Teacher Wishlist outreach. Strong fit for kids interested in education funding + nonprofit operations.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit donorschoose.org/we-help-classrooms. Year-round availability. Project Champion role can be started by reaching out to teachers at your school.

opportunities.name: Adaptive Sports Foundation Volunteer
opportunities.description: Adaptive Sports Foundation has 100+ chapters nationally providing adaptive sports for individuals with disabilities. HS volunteer roles include adaptive ski instruction (with training), adaptive cycling event support, adaptive sailing assistant, and Wounded Warrior Sports days. Strong fit for kids interested in adaptive sports, occupational therapy, or special education careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit adaptivesportsfoundation.org/volunteer. Find your local chapter; most welcome HS volunteers with training. Adaptive ski programs typically Dec-Mar; summer programs Jun-Aug.

opportunities.name: GLSEN Student Network
opportunities.description: GLSEN works to ensure safe + affirming K-12 schools for LGBTQ+ students. HS volunteer roles include Day of Silence (annual April) organizing, GSA chapter founding/leadership, No Name-Calling Week (Jan), and GLSEN Student Action Awards advocacy. Strong fit for LGBTQ+ allies + students interested in education policy + civil rights careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit glsen.org/student-action. Day of Silence annual April; year-round GSA support. Apply Aug-Sep for school year.

opportunities.name: GSA Network HS Chapter Leadership
opportunities.description: GSA Network supports 4,000+ Gender + Sexualities Alliance student clubs nationally. HS GSA chapter leadership roles include club chartering, peer-to-peer support training, anti-bullying campaigns, and Trans Day of Visibility (annual March 31) event coordination. Strong fit for LGBTQ+ youth + allies interested in civil rights + community organizing careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit gsanetwork.org/start-a-gsa to start a club at your HS. GSA Network supports clubs in CA + NY + TX with regional staff. Year-round.

opportunities.name: International Rescue Committee (IRC) Youth Volunteer
opportunities.description: IRC resettles refugees in 28 US cities + provides global humanitarian assistance. HS volunteer roles include refugee youth tutoring, post-arrival adjustment support, ESL conversation partner (16+), school enrollment assistance, and World Refugee Day event organizing. Strong fit for kids interested in refugee policy + international development.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit rescue.org/take-action and find your local IRC office (28 US cities). Most welcome HS volunteers; ESL conversation partner role typically 16+. Year-round.

opportunities.name: Lutheran Immigration + Refugee Service Volunteer
opportunities.description: LIRS is one of the largest refugee resettlement networks in the US. HS volunteer roles include New American Welcome Center support, refugee youth tutoring, Walk for Welcome event organizing (annual June), and refugee policy advocacy. Strong faith-based context. Strong fit for kids interested in refugee resettlement + faith-based humanitarian careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit lirs.org/get-involved. Find your local LIRS affiliate. Year-round availability. Walk for Welcome June.

opportunities.name: HIAS (Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society) Volunteer
opportunities.description: HIAS is the world's oldest refugee agency (founded 1881), originally Jewish but now serves refugees globally. HS volunteer roles include refugee post-arrival support, Hebrew School + Sunday School refugee education, advocacy on US refugee policy, and HIAS Volunteer Days at synagogues. Strong fit for Jewish-American + interfaith students interested in refugee + immigration advocacy.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit hias.org/take-action. Many synagogue-affiliated programs welcome HS volunteers. Year-round availability.

opportunities.name: Wheelchair Sports Federation Junior Volunteer
opportunities.organization: US Wheelchair Sports Federation + State Affiliates
opportunities.description: US Wheelchair Sports Federation supports adaptive wheelchair sports nationally + state-level. HS volunteer roles include wheelchair basketball game day support, wheelchair tennis tournament volunteer, wheelchair rugby event coordination, and Push America youth ambassadorship (Pi Kappa Phi fraternity). Strong fit for kids interested in adaptive sports + occupational therapy careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Search 'wheelchair basketball [your city]' or 'adaptive sports [your state]' to find local affiliate. Year-round availability with peak basketball Nov-Mar + tennis Mar-Aug.

opportunities.name: Easterseals Junior Volunteer
opportunities.description: Easterseals provides services to people with disabilities, families, veterans + seniors at 76+ affiliates nationally. HS volunteer roles include Day Camp Counselor (with disability awareness training), Veteran's Affairs office support, sensory-friendly event organizing, and Walk With Me event coordination (annual May). Strong fit for kids interested in special education + therapy careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit easterseals.com/get-involved. Find your local Easterseals affiliate. Year-round availability with peak camp summer + Walk With Me May.

opportunities.name: Autism Speaks Volunteer + U Walk
opportunities.description: Autism Speaks is the largest autism advocacy organization in the US. HS volunteer roles include Autism Speaks Walk event coordination, U Walk school chapter founding, Autism Speaks Light It Up Blue (annual April 2 World Autism Day), and family resource advocacy. Strong fit for kids interested in autism research + special education + behavioral therapy careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit autismspeaks.org/take-action. U Walk school chapters can be started year-round. Autism Speaks Walk events Spring/Fall.

opportunities.name: PFLAG Junior Ally + Family Volunteer
opportunities.organization: PFLAG (Parents, Families and Friends of Lesbians and Gays)
opportunities.description: PFLAG has 400+ chapters nationally supporting LGBTQ+ youth + families. HS volunteer roles include local chapter event support, Pride Month event coordination (annual June), school visit programs (HS Outreach), and Family Acceptance Project support. Strong fit for LGBTQ+ allies + students interested in family support + advocacy.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit pflag.org/find-a-chapter. Most chapters welcome HS volunteers. Pride Month events June; year-round support.

opportunities.name: Feeding South Florida (Miami + Broward + Palm Beach)
opportunities.description: Feeding South Florida is the largest food bank in Florida (covers Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, Monroe). HS volunteer roles include warehouse food sorting, Mobile Pantry distribution, Backpack Program (weekend kid meals), and BAGS Mealbox holiday distribution. Year-round with peak holiday season Nov-Dec.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit feedingsouthflorida.org/get-involved. Year-round availability. Apply via online portal.

opportunities.name: Atlanta Community Food Bank Volunteer
opportunities.description: Atlanta Community Food Bank serves 29 counties in Georgia + parts of Alabama. HS volunteer roles include warehouse food sorting (12+), MarketShare community grocery, Kids in Need backpack distribution, and Atlanta-area food drive coordination. Year-round with strong school + community partnership.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit acfb.org/get-involved/volunteer. Year-round availability. Apply via online portal.

opportunities.name: NC Conservation Council Junior Volunteer
opportunities.description: North Carolina Conservation Council protects NC natural resources + advocates for conservation policy. HS volunteer roles include forestry restoration days, Outer Banks beach cleanup, Wild Carolina youth ambassador, and conservation advocacy at NC General Assembly. Strong fit for NC kids interested in environmental science + policy careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit ncconservation.org/get-involved. Year-round campaign volunteer roles. Apply via online portal.

opportunities.name: Arizona Humane Society Junior Volunteer
opportunities.description: Arizona Humane Society is one of Arizona's largest animal welfare orgs (Phoenix, Tucson, Mesa). HS volunteer roles include shelter dog socialization, cat adoption events, Tortoise + Chelonia Conservation, and Senior Pet matching. Strong fit for AZ kids interested in animal welfare + veterinary careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit azhumane.org/volunteer. Year-round availability. Apply via online portal — under 16 typically with parent/guardian.

opportunities.name: Colorado Outdoor Volunteer Connection
opportunities.description: VOC is Colorado's largest outdoor volunteer org. HS volunteer roles include 14er trail restoration, Rocky Mountain National Park preservation, Colorado Trails Day events, and youth-led conservation crew programs. Strong fit for CO kids interested in environmental fieldwork + park ranger careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit voc.org/volunteer. Year-round availability with peak summer (Jun-Sep). Apply via online portal.

opportunities.name: Cincinnati Children's Hospital + Akron Children's Hospital Junior Volunteer (Ohio)
opportunities.organization: Cincinnati Children's Hospital + Akron Children's Hospital
opportunities.description: Both Cincinnati Children's + Akron Children's hospitals run robust junior volunteer programs for HS students 14-18. Roles include playroom support, family lounge assistance, gift shop staffing, way-finding, and waiting room hospitality. Strong fit for OH kids interested in pediatrics + pre-med careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Cincinnati Children's: cincinnatichildrens.org/volunteer. Akron Children's: akronchildrens.org/volunteer. Apply Feb-Apr for summer programs.

opportunities.name: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) Junior Volunteer
opportunities.description: CHOP is Pennsylvania's #1 pediatric hospital. HS volunteer roles include playroom support, family resource center, gift shop, transport assistance, and way-finding. Highly competitive — 50-100 hours/year minimum. Strong fit for PA kids interested in pediatrics + pre-med careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit chop.edu/volunteer. Apply Feb-Apr for summer programs. Background check + immunization records required.

opportunities.name: Second Harvest Heartland Twin Cities (Minnesota)
opportunities.description: Second Harvest Heartland is one of the largest food banks in the Upper Midwest (Minnesota, North + South Dakota, parts of Wisconsin). HS volunteer roles include warehouse food sorting, Backpack Program, Mobile Food Shelf distribution, and Hunger Action Month (Sep) coordination. Strong fit for MN kids interested in food justice.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit 2harvest.org/volunteer. Year-round availability. Apply via online portal.

opportunities.name: Oregon Food Bank Network
opportunities.description: Oregon Food Bank serves 22 regional food banks across Oregon + Clark County WA. HS volunteer roles include warehouse food sorting, Repack events (sorting bulk into family-size), Mobile Pantry distribution, and Hunger to Health Coalition advocacy. Strong fit for OR kids interested in food justice + public health careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit oregonfoodbank.org/volunteer. Year-round availability. Apply via online portal.

opportunities.name: American Heart Association School Programs + Walk
opportunities.description: AHA runs HS volunteer programs nationally. HS roles include Kids Heart Challenge + American Heart Challenge school fundraising, Heart Walk event coordination, AHA School Site Coordinator, and CPR/AED instructor (with AHA training). Strong fit for kids interested in cardiology + emergency medicine + nursing careers.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit heart.org/volunteer. Year-round availability with peak Heart Walk events Spring/Fall. Apply via online portal.

opportunities.name: Zoo Miami Conservation Teen Scientist
opportunities.description: Zoo Miami's flagship teen volunteer program for ages 14-18 in or entering high school. Volunteers train in zoo operations including kitchen prep of animal diets, the giraffe feeding platform, education stations, and guest interpretation. Strong fit for pre-vet, biology, conservation, and zoology pathways. Commitment: 15 days during summer + 2 days/month during school year. Selected by application; alumni cite it as one of the most prestigious teen programs in South Florida.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit zoomiami.org/volunteer and review the Conservation Teen Scientist application window (typically opens late winter for summer cohort). Application includes essay + recommendation. Selective.

opportunities.name: Jacksonville Zoo & Gardens ZooTeens
opportunities.description: ZooTeens is Jacksonville Zoo's flagship youth-development volunteer program for ages 14-18 currently completing high school. Roles include conservation stations, education camps, guest engagement, and behind-the-scenes animal-care support. Multi-year commitment encouraged; tiered advancement model. Annual NE Florida cohort intake. Junior volunteer roles available for ages 13-17 throughout the year for shorter-term involvement.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply via jacksonvillezoo.org/teens. Application windows typically open in spring for summer cohort. Mandatory orientation + uniform fee.

opportunities.name: The Florida Aquarium Junior Camp Counselor
opportunities.description: Tampa-based aquarium's selective summer-only volunteer program for high schoolers ages 14-17. Junior Camp Counselors support summer marine-science day camps for younger students. Six-week commitment June 1 - July 31; minimum 40 hours over the summer. Excellent fit for marine biology, environmental science, and education-pathway students. Education Volunteer roles also available year-round for older teens.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply at flaquarium.org/gift-give/volunteer/volunteer-opportunities/junior-camp-counselor-volunteer. Application typically opens January-March for summer term.

opportunities.name: Nicklaus Children's Hospital Teen Volunteer
opportunities.description: South Florida's premier pediatric hospital teen volunteer program in Miami (3100 SW 62nd Ave). High school students fulfill 6-month / 80-hour minimum commitment, one 3-hour shift per week. Roles include patient family support, gift shop, way-finding, and clinic admin. Highly competitive — first-come/first-served until cohort capacity reached. Strong pre-med / pre-nursing track record. Required: immunization records (MMR, Varicella, Tdap, TB, flu), birth certificate, recent school report.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit nicklauschildrens.org/about-us/volunteer-resources/teen-applicant. Complete online welcome orientation, then in-person interview at Volunteer Resources.

opportunities.name: AdventHealth Central Florida Volunteer Services
opportunities.description: Central Florida's largest hospital system runs structured volunteer programs across Orlando-area campuses (AdventHealth Orlando, Winter Park, Celebration, Apopka, Altamonte). Minimum age 16. Teen-and-college-student-focused programs include cuddler/family liaison, way-finding, gift shop, surgical waiting support, and outpatient clinic admin. Strong pipeline for pre-med / pre-nursing / health-admin tracks. AdventHealth Tampa runs a parallel program.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply via adventhealth.com/community-benefit/central-florida/volunteer. Background check, immunization records, and orientation required.

opportunities.name: Frameworks Teens In Action (TIA)
opportunities.description: Frameworks' flagship 10-month civic-engagement program for Hillsborough County high schoolers grades 9-12. Monthly leadership workshops paired with weekly volunteer placements at partner nonprofits. Teens earn up to 36 community-service hours that count toward Florida's Bright Futures Scholarship requirements. Program emphasizes social-emotional skills, equity, and applied civic engagement. Strong fit for civic-leadership / public-policy pathways.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply at myframeworks.org/teens-in-action. Annual application window typically opens late summer for fall cohort start.

opportunities.name: Humane Society of Tampa Bay Junior Camp Counselor + Teen Volunteer
opportunities.description: Tampa Bay's largest no-kill animal welfare org. Two teen tracks: Junior Camp Counselor (14-15, completed 9th grade) supports summer animal-camp programming for younger kids; Teen Volunteer (16+) covers shelter operations, adoption support, dog walking, cat socialization. High school + college students can earn up to 40 volunteer hours/week during summer. Multi-month commitment encouraged.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit humanesocietytampabay.org/how-to-help/volunteer for current application windows. Junior Camp Counselor applications typically open in spring for summer cohort.

opportunities.name: Habitat for Humanity Greater Orlando & Osceola County
opportunities.organization: Habitat for Humanity Greater Orlando & Osceola County
opportunities.description: Build-site volunteer program serving the Orlando / Osceola affordable-housing developments (Holden Heights and Parramore neighborhoods). Volunteers must be 16+ for build sites; some tasks restricted to 18+. No prior construction experience required — site supervisors provide on-the-job training. Tasks span wall raising, painting, cabinet installation, landscaping. Strong fit for community-development, civil-engineering, and architecture-pathway students. Group / Team Build options for school clubs.
opportunities.howToStart: Sign up at habitatorlando.org/volunteer for individual or Team Build days. Closed-toe shoes required. Tools/safety gear provided.

opportunities.name: Florida Oceanographic Society Teen Environmental Volunteer
opportunities.description: Stuart-based marine-science nonprofit (Treasure Coast). Teen track includes Exhibit Guide (interpretation at invertebrate touch tanks + Ocean EcoCenter) and Independent Beach Cleanup (flexible app-based scheduling). Exhibit Guide application requires 1-page essay on FL coastal ecosystems + 2 teacher recommendations including science teacher. Strong fit for marine-bio, environmental-science, and education pathways.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit floridaocean.org/teen-environmental-opportunities to apply. Exhibit Guide is selective; Beach Cleanup is open enrollment via Clean Swell app.

opportunities.name: Sanibel-Captiva Conservation Foundation (SCCF) Volunteer
opportunities.description: Sanibel & Captiva Islands' premier conservation foundation. Year-round opportunities include sea turtle nest monitoring, shorebird observation, oyster reef restoration, mangrove planting, beach stewardship, and native-species planting via the Coastal Watch program. Open to all ages; minors must be accompanied by a parent/guardian for fieldwork. Excellent fit for marine-bio, ecology, and wildlife-conservation students.
opportunities.subregion: Sanibel / Captiva / Lee County / Southwest Florida
opportunities.howToStart: Browse opportunities at sccf.org/get-involved/volunteer-opportunities. Sea turtle monitoring season runs May-October; mangrove + oyster restoration year-round.

opportunities.name: Coral Restoration Foundation (Key Largo)
opportunities.description: Key Largo-based nonprofit, the world's largest coral-reef restoration org. Land-based volunteer roles (greeting visitors, warehouse, building coral trees) open to teens; water-based Dive Team experiences require open-water certification (typically 15+, parental consent for minors). One-day and two-day Dive Team commitments available, plus longer-term monthly diving for certified volunteers. Iconic for marine-bio, oceanography, and coral-reef-research-track students.
opportunities.subregion: Key Largo / Florida Keys / Monroe County
opportunities.howToStart: Apply at coralrestoration.org/volunteer. Land-based application is rolling; Dive Program requires Open Water cert + signed waiver. Lodging is on-volunteer.

opportunities.name: Florida Holocaust Museum Volunteer
opportunities.description: St. Petersburg-based museum (one of the three largest Holocaust museums in the U.S., ~220 active volunteers). Teen + adult volunteer roles span gallery docent, education program assistant, library/archives helper, and event support. Strong fit for history, social-justice, education, and museum-studies pathway students. Cohort training plus ongoing professional development.
opportunities.subregion: St. Petersburg / Tampa Bay / Pinellas County
opportunities.howToStart: Visit thefhm.org and navigate to Get Involved → Volunteer to start the application. Cohort training schedule published quarterly.

opportunities.name: Volunteer Florida AmeriCorps + Community Service
opportunities.organization: Volunteer Florida (Governor's Commission on Volunteerism and Community Service)
opportunities.description: Florida's statewide commission supporting AmeriCorps placements + community-service grant programs across all 67 counties. AmeriCorps Florida programs accept high school graduates 17+ for service-year terms (education, conservation, disaster response, public health). For high-school-age students, the commission's volunteer.volunteerflorida.org portal is the canonical search hub for vetted local opportunities. Strong civic-engagement and federal-service-pathway value.
opportunities.howToStart: For AmeriCorps placements (17+): apply via volunteerflorida.org/americorps. For volunteer search across all 67 counties: visit volunteer.volunteerflorida.org and filter by location/cause/age.
